requirement_text.REQ-036: GitHub issue #68. Pending-request urgency flag at T-48h and honest auto-decline at registration close. Closes JOURNEY-AUDIT J3, implementing STORY-DETAILS B6 (member side, "nobody waits past the event") and F3 (organizer side, "requests still pending 48h before the start are flagged urgent"). depends_on: REQ-035 (merged). Two scheduled jobs registered via the existing startScheduledJobs() runner (apps/bot/src/scheduler/runner.ts) -- no new scheduling mechanism. URGENCY at T-48h before starts_at: every event with requests still admission='requested' surfaces those to that event's organizers as urgent, via a mechanism the design states concretely enough to be checked (a notification, a list marker, or both). AUTO-DECLINE at registration_closes_at: every remaining 'requested' registration -> 'rejected', person told honestly (no wording implying personal judgment), offered the SAME onward path REQ-035 established. registration_closes_at IS NULL: the design must state explicitly what happens (an ends_at fallback, or no auto-decline with urgency as sole backstop) and justify it -- no schema change permitted to make the null case go away. IDEMPOTENCY (S9): both sends through REQ-025's ledger with distinct kinds; the auto-decline's own state write is a SEPARATE, independently self-guarding mechanism (a row already 'rejected' can never match the still-'requested' selection filter again) -- the design must state these are TWO mechanisms, not one. Both sends are transactional, reach broadcast_opt_in=false users, skip blocked=true users. Each auto-decline writes exactly one AuditLog row with actor_user_id=NULL (system-initiated). Copy is honest/blame-free, same treatment as REQ-014/032, provisional pending product owner. AC4 is a genuine restart-safety test (kill mid-batch, restart, re-run: exactly the original send count, no further transitions) -- the design must trace that this actually holds given the chosen mechanism.

task.description: WF-02 Step 1 (Design) for REQ-036, on branch feature/WF02-REQ-036 (verified branch matches, commit f6468ff at run start). Produced docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md mapping all 8 acceptance criteria to concrete design elements. Key resolutions: (1) URGENCY mechanism = BOTH a push notification to ONE deterministically-chosen organizer per chapter (new NotificationKind 'pending_request_urgent', reusing sendLedgeredNotification completely unchanged) AND a list marker (new isUrgent field on the existing PendingRequestListItem/listPendingRequestsForOrganizer, computed fresh on every render via a new pure predicate isRequestUrgent in domain/event.ts, mirroring isAutoPromotionHalted's exact T-24h-boundary shape at a 48h threshold) -- traced explicitly why only ONE organizer is pushed (notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) has no recipient column, so fanning the same registration+kind out to N organizers would let only the first organizer's call win the ledger insert; the list marker independently covers every other organizer who opens /requests, regardless of push delivery). (2) registration_closes_at IS NULL resolved as an ends_at fallback (not 'no auto-decline'), justified directly from STORY-DETAILS B6's own 'nobody waits past the event' language -- no column added. (3) Two-mechanism idempotency traced explicitly and named as genuinely distinct: Mechanism 1 (notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), guards whether a message sends) vs Mechanism 2 (decideRejectionOutcome's existing admission!=='requested' branch, reused UNCHANGED from REQ-035, guards whether the row transitions) -- neither depends on the other. (4) Auto-decline write reuses decideRejectionOutcome unchanged but introduces a NEW transactional writer, autoDeclineRequest (no organizerUserId parameter, actorUserId always NULL, new audit action 'registration.auto_decline' distinct from REQ-035's 'registration.reject') -- reasoned as necessary because rejectRequest's signature has no branch that omits a human organizer id, and changing an already-merged/tested function's contract was rejected in favor of a dedicated writer, the same 'distinct action per branch' discipline REQ-035 already used for approve vs. approve_override. (5) Restart-safety (AC4) traced through an explicit kill-mid-batch scenario across three candidates, showing the send count and transition count both come out identical across a kill+restart, using only the two already-existing mechanisms -- no new restart-recovery logic added. A narrower single-candidate torn-write window (state committed, notification never attempted) is named explicitly in Open Question 3 as the same already-accepted class of risk REQ-035's own approve/reject sequencing carries, not newly introduced here, and not covered by any AC in this requirement's list. (6) Two new NotificationKind literals ('pending_request_urgent', 'registration_auto_declined'), both reusing sendLedgeredNotification unchanged -- no new send primitive. Confirmed independently: no schema change anywhere in this design (every write/read targets an existing column with its existing type, including audit_log.actor_user_id's already-nullable, already-commented system-actor case) -- DATA-DESIGNER is NOT needed for this run.
acceptance_criteria: An event exactly 48h from starts_at with two admission='requested' registrations surfaces both to that event's organizers via the named mechanism; an event more than 48h out surfaces nothing; both timings are run.

At registration_closes_at, every remaining admission='requested' registration becomes 'rejected' and each person receives exactly one message; an already-approved and an already-rejected registration are untouched.
The auto-decline message states that no decision was reached in time and contains no wording attributing the outcome to the person's own merits, and offers the upcoming-events list as an onward path.
Running the auto-decline job, killing the process, restarting it, and running the job again for the same event delivers exactly the original number of messages and performs no further transitions.
An event whose registration_closes_at is NULL behaves exactly as the design artefact states for that case -- no unhandled crash, no undocumented silent skip, no new column.
Each auto-decline writes exactly one audit_log row, actor_user_id NULL.
Both the urgency message and the auto-decline message reach a user with broadcast_opt_in=false and reach neither a user with blocked=true.

Every user-facing string added by this requirement resolves through the catalog mechanism in both ru and en; the handoff result records the auto-decline wording as provisional pending the product owner.

result.summary: Produced docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md (9 sections, full AC map in section 8, open questions in section 7). Confirmed no schema change is needed anywhere in this design -- every write/read targets an existing column with its existing type (registrations.admission, events.startsAt/endsAt/registrationClosesAt, audit_log.actorUserId already nullable with a comment already anticipating this exact system-initiated case, notification_ledger's existing UNIQUE(registration_id, kind)). DATA-DESIGNER is NOT dispatched for this run. Design gate reviewers should check in particular: (a) the traced reasoning for why only ONE organizer receives the push notification rather than a fan-out to every organizer of the chapter, given notification_ledger has no per-recipient column (section 2.2); (b) the ends_at fallback for registration_closes_at IS NULL, justified from the requirement's own 'nobody waits past the event' language rather than invented (section 3.1); (c) the explicit two-mechanism idempotency trace (section 0.3/3.4) and the restart-safety walkthrough (section 4); (d) that no implementation code appears anywhere -- every new function is a signature ending in ';' plus prose/table rules, matching this codebase's own REQ-035 precedent artefact's style.
issues: OPEN (Open Question 1 in the design): a chapter with zero assigned organizers at T-48h receives no push (getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter returns null, the job skips that candidate with no ledger row written) -- the list marker independently covers a later-assigned organizer since it is computed fresh on every render, but this is named explicitly rather than silently assumed to never happen.
OPEN (Open Question 2): exact file placement of getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter (domain/registration.ts vs domain/event.ts) is left to BACKEND-DEV, no behavioral consequence either way.

OPEN (Open Question 3): the narrow single-candidate torn-write window (autoDeclineRequest's state transition commits, then a crash occurs before sendLedgeredNotification is even invoked) would leave that one registrant permanently un-notified -- named explicitly as the same already-accepted risk class REQ-035's own approve/reject write-then-notify sequencing carries, not a new risk introduced here, and not required to be closed by any AC in this requirement's list.
OPEN (Open Question 4): urgentMarker's exact rendered placement/format in the /requests list is BACKEND-DEV's implementation choice -- no AC pins an exact visual format.

REQUIRED FOR BACKEND-DEV'S OWN HANDOFF (restated per the requirement's own instruction, REQ-014/032 precedent): the two new catalog leaves (organizerRequests.urgentMarker, organizerRequests.urgentNotification, autoDecline.notification) are provisional placeholder copy; BACKEND-DEV's result.summary must record this as pending the product owner, the same way REQ-014/REQ-032's implementation handoffs already did.
